prior_year_events.impact_description: The Syndicate's exposure to the large losses incurred during 2022 includes the Russia/Ukraine Conflict. A management margin of $36.8m net of reinsurance and reinstatement premiums has been made. Given the nature of the Russia/Ukraine Conflict, the ultimate losses relating to the event are subject to a high degree of uncertainty. In response, the Syndicate has booked prudent reserves reflecting our exposure.

The 2020 year of account closed on 31 December 2022 with a profit of $27.6m. This includes movement on the closed years of account and equates to a profit of 15.2% of capacity. All classes have made positive contributions to the underwriting balance with the year of account benefiting from relatively benign catastrophe experience, together with favourable development on prior years.
In 2021, we retained the elevated status due to the social inflation risk within claims. This implies adverse development, particularly for longer tail lines.

Inflation across the U.S. and Europe reaching its highest level for many years, leading to a detailed analysis on the impact of inflation rates to ultimate losses and reserve levels, with the risk trending upwards.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a significant gross prior year strengthening of $146.569 million, representing 123.3% of its opening gross claims outstanding. This adverse development was primarily driven by the impact of the Russia/Ukraine Conflict, which led to booking prudent reserves, and general economic and social inflation trends affecting ultimate losses. However, the 2020 year of account, which closed in 2022, showed favourable development across all classes due to benign catastrophe experience.
